tldr: Hugging Face opened the thread on Nov 20 by training a LoRA adapter that fits a model to its harness, raising Qwen3.8-27B's Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass@1 from 39% to 55% on half the tokens. On Nov 23 Jcode, an open-source Rust harness, shifted the lever to running parallel agents on one repo with a server that coordinates file changes.
whats_new: Delegent, an arXiv harness built on Claude Code, keeps a frontier model in charge and hands easy subtasks to a small local model, reporting 67% lower frontier cost on long-horizon coding and 59% on agentic search.
why_it_matters: Three separate teams treat the harness, not the model, as the tuning surface for agent cost and pass rate: adapter training, parallel orchestration, and frontier-to-local delegation.

status.detail: Each result is self-reported by its authors on its own benchmark; no item yet compares the three approaches on a shared task.

beats.headline: Hugging Face trains a LoRA adapter to fit a model to its harness
beats.summary: RL on Qwen3.8-27B with the Pi harness: Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass@1 39% to 55%, average tokens 2.9K to 1.5K.

beats.headline: Jcode runs parallel coding agents on one repo from a Rust harness
beats.summary: A coordinating server notifies agents of file changes and handles messaging between them; no benchmark numbers attached.

beats.headline: Delegent routes easy subtasks from a frontier model to a local one
beats.summary: Built on Claude Code; reports 67% lower frontier cost on long-horizon coding and 59% on agentic search.

open_questions: Does a harness adapter trained for Pi keep its Terminal-Bench gain when the same model runs in a different harness?
Does Delegent's frontier-cost cut hold once local-model latency and hardware cost are counted?
Does Jcode publish pass-rate or throughput numbers against a single-agent harness?
Does any independent group reproduce these gains on a shared benchmark such as Terminal-Bench?
take_for_builders: Before switching models to cut agent cost, benchmark harness changes on your own tasks: log frontier-token spend per subtask and test routing the cheap ones to a local model.
